chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ja'far ibn Uthman, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer and others, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The heart happens to be, at a given moment of the day or night, in a state where there is neither disbelief nor faith, like a worn-out garment.'
He said, 'Then he said to me: Do you not find that within yourself?' He said: 'The spot (or mark) appears from Allah in the heart, according to what He wills, of disbelief and faith.'
A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umeyr, [narrated] similarly.

key_terms.الثَّوْبِ الْخَلَقِ: The worn-out garment (metaphor for an intermediate, indeterminate state)
key_terms.النُّكْتَةُ: The spot/mark (indicating a decisive spiritual state or characteristic)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual state of the heart between faith and disbelief according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the context of Chapter 184 on 'Omissions of the heart' (Niqdan al-Qalb), Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) illustrates the fluidity of spiritual states, where the heart oscillates between faith and disbelief like a worn garment. This Hadith highlights the concept of *Nuktah* (a decisive spiritual mark or impression) that Allah places in the heart, solidifying its trajectory toward either *Iman* or *Kufr*. It underscores the dynamic nature of the soul's condition, emphasizing that one's current state is not necessarily permanent until that decisive mark is set by Divine Will.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ja’far Bin Usman, from Sama’at, from Abu Baseer and someone else who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The heart happens to be such during a time of the day and the night that there is neither a Kufr (disbelief) in it nor Emān, like the newly-created garment’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘Then heasws said to me: ‘But, do you not find that from yourself?’ Heasws said: ‘The spot appears from Allahazwj in the heart with whatever Allahazwj has so Desired it to be, from Kufr and the Emān’.
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Abu Umeyr – smilar to it.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from la’ far ibn ‘Uthman from Sama’a from abu Basir and others who has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘The heart in certain hours of the night and day has no disbelief or belief in it and it is like an old mg.’
The narrator has said that the Imam then asked, ‘Do you not find that in yourself? Then there is a dot from Allah in the heart of the kind that He wills in the form of disbelief or belief.’”
A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn abu ‘Umayr a similar Hadith.
